assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ is a textbook case of a simple stochastic growth equation whose scaling exponents and Tracy-Widom-type fluctuation statistics are universal across a very wide class of non-equilibrium systems (interface growth, directed polymers, exclusion processes, turbulent liquid crystals). It is the kind of clean, analysable model with a surprisingly general mechanism that I weigh most heavily, and its exact solutions linked non-equilibrium physics to random-matrix theory.
assessment.attribution: The 1986 equation is due to Kardar, Parisi and Zhang; Parisi is not in the credited names and, as I recall, already received a prize for other work, so Kardar and Zhang are the natural theory pair. Takeuchi and Sano provided the decisive experimental confirmation of the universal distributions. The exact-solution contributions (Johansson, Spohn, Sasamoto, Amir-Corwin-Quastel and others) are not credited here, which complicates a fully fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Theory dates from 1986, exact solutions from about 2000 onward, and experimental confirmation in turbulent liquid crystals from 2010, followed by cold-atom and other realisations. The interpretation is stable and independently confirmed, so the timing is mature.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the equation or on the exact solutions and universality class is unresolved.
I have not independently verified the credit chain for the exact solutions, and the omission of mathematical-physics contributors weakens the attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials: a tunable flat-band platform with correlated insulators and superconductivity. It rests on a simple, general mechanism, interference of two lattices with a small twist, and has spawned a large field including twisted TMDs and fractional Chern insulators.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 continuum-model prediction of flat bands at the magic angle. Jarillo-Herrero's group did the 2018 experiments showing correlated insulators and superconductivity. Theory plus experiment is a clean pairing. Contributions such as Cao's experimental work as lead author and others on the theory side are not in the supplied names, which is an open credit question.
assessment.maturity: Prediction in 2011 and experiments from 2018 are well reproduced by many groups. Nature of the superconducting pairing is still debated, but the discovery itself is solid. Timing is arguably early but acceptable.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Recognition of the junior experimental first author and of the broader twistronics community could complicate a three-person split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture offers a unifying, nearly critical, mechanism for the rigidity transition of grains, foams, emulsions and glasses, with universal scaling near the transition point. It is exactly the sort of simple cross-system idea that I value, and it links soft matter to glass physics and to the geometry of random packings.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel's 1998 jamming phase diagram is the conceptual origin. The subsequent work of O'Hern, Silbert, Liu and Nagel on point J gave the quantitative scaling. Their credit is concentrated and clear, with the caveat that the infinite-dimension mean-field solution (Parisi, Zamponi, Charbonneau and others) built on it.
assessment.maturity: The framework is widely adopted and tested in simulations and experiments, but the exact nature of point J as a true critical point and its relation to the glass transition are still under debate. The prize may be a little premature.
uncertainties: Whether jamming is a genuine phase transition with a rigorous universality class is not fully settled.
The relation to the glass transition and to mean-field theory leaves some credit ambiguity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices serve as clean, tunable realisations of Hubbard-type models. The Mott insulator transition, quantum gas microscopy and fermionic Hubbard physics allow direct tests of many-body theory. This connects statistical physics, simulation and computation.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch and Zoller proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation. Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-Mott transition, and Esslinger led fermionic work. Four names are supplied but the prize permits three. The proposed three are an arguable split, and the choice between Greiner and Esslinger is hard.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature with many independent confirmations, though it is partly overlapped by earlier cold-atom prizes for laser cooling and BEC. The scientific payoff in solving open many-body problems is still emerging.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes on laser cooling and Bose-Einstein condensation may reduce the novelty weight.
Exclusion of Markus Greiner, or of the theory pioneers Jaksch and others, is a fairness problem.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators are a major conceptual advance: bulk-boundary correspondence yields protected edge and surface states in time-reversal-symmetric materials, with deep links to topology and to the earlier quantum Hall prize lineage.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall effect in 2005. Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells in 2007, following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are not credited, and three-dimensional topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele, Hasan, Moore, Balents) are also omitted, so allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: The theory and experiment are confirmed repeatedly, and the field is mature. The 2016 prize on topological phases partly reduces the room for a further topology prize, though it did not cover this.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal and for the 3D case lies outside the supplied names.
Possible overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 experimentally confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and completed the Standard Model. The significance is very high, and it is a clean, decisive discovery.
assessment.attribution: The theory prize was awarded in 2013 to Englert and Higgs. The experimental discovery was done by collaborations of thousands. Proposers and spokespersons such as Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee led the conception and construction of the detectors, but it remains a difficult attribution because the prize rules favour individuals rather than collaborations.
assessment.maturity: The discovery is long confirmed and is stable, with coupling measurements consistent with the Standard Model. Recognition is fully mature, even overdue.
uncertainties: Attribution to three individuals for a collaboration of thousands is intrinsically arbitrary and could be viewed as unfair.
I would defer to colleagues in experimental particle physics on the proper candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via the magic-wavelength idea, deliver fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, opening tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. The importance for precision physics is large.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group demonstrated best-in-class performance in strontium. This two-person credit is quite clear, with other contributors in Paris, Boulder and elsewhere not essential for the central idea.
assessment.maturity: Performance has been confirmed by several independent labs and is stable. The redefinition of the second is not yet complete, but the discovery is established. Timing is reasonable, although precision metrology was recognised in 2005 and 2012.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock-related prizes (frequency combs, ion trapping) could reduce priority.
Whether the community sees the clock as a discovery or as an engineering refinement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Geometric phases, from the Aharonov-Bohm effect to Berry's adiabatic phase, are a remarkably general mechanism that underlies Bloch-band topology, the quantum Hall effect, polarisation of solids and molecular conical intersections. It is foundational in the spirit of papers that already contained much of what followed.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm (1959) and Berry (1984) are credited; Bohm is deceased and cannot be honoured, and Pancharatnam and Simon also made antecedent or related contributions. Two living laureates is a workable configuration, though a priority debate exists.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation of both effects is long established, so the maturity is complete. If anything the concern is that the prize is long delayed and that much of the impact has already been attributed to later topological-matter prizes.
uncertainties: Priority questions (Pancharatnam, Ehrenberg-Siday, Simon) complicate attribution.
The case may be seen as largely subsumed into the 2016 and 1985 prizes.
Whether the committee would treat these as a single compound discovery or as two separate ones.
